liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Big Railroad Blues** (1 review): Jerry rips the end of Big Railroad Blues, a first set standout [29]
- **Let it Grow** (1 review): Remarkable jam in Let It Grow highlights an otherwise mediocre show [31]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-10-09.nak300.carpenter.wise.andrewf.81386.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 23 songs; 154 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]. Said about its sound: Tape-deck malfunction caused a high-pitched whine near the start of Big Railroad [1]
- **gd1984-10-09.168001.beyer.m160.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 22 songs; 154 min [6]
- **gd1984-10-09.nak100.holtz-bolton.GEMS.96737.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 151 min; rated 4.62/5 by 8 [10]. Said about its sound: Listener believes this is the best-sounding and latest complete show available; Sound is crystal clear and well defined, though low end needs boosting; Sound requires significant equalization to become listenable to this reviewer [25][26][31]
- **gd1984-10-09.senn421.pauline.miller.91410.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 151 min; rated 4.2/5 by 5 [11]. Said about its sound: Listener calls this the best-sounding source available, praising the transfer work; Recording sounds boomy and noisy, typical of east coast arena shows [22][23]
- **gd1984-10-09.beyerm88.suraci.77880.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 146 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [12]. Said about its sound: Excellent front-of-house recording with strong, thick sound and very good imaging [24]

## Around the show

- Crowd went wild for the first Smokestack Lightnin' performance in ages [22]
- Band performed a tribute on John Lennon's birthday, from Dancin' to Revolution [23]
- Jerry and Phil listen to each other closely during this performance [28]
- Encore Revolution dedicated to Sandy, a friend of the tapers [2]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-10-09.nak300.carpenter.wise.andrewf.81386.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Ted Carpenter; transferred by Jim Wise and Andrew F.; source: FOB, Nakamichi CM-300's with CP-4 shotgun capsules > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell UD-XLII's, no Dolby [1]. Also: Drop-out in He's Gone patched with ShnID-77880 from 3:07 to 3:17; Tape flip in Drums patched with ShnID-77880 from 1:57 to 2:37 [1]
- **gd1984-10-09.168001.beyer.m160.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Beyer M160 mics > Sony D5M (Maxell XLII-S) [6]. Also: Sennheiser 421 source supplies a 6:26 patch in the song Drums [6]
- **gd1984-10-09.nak100.holtz-bolton.GEMS.96737.flac16**: taped by Greg Holtz and Tony Bolton; transferred by Jamie Waddell; source: Location: FOB Jerry's side roughly 10-12 feet right of center,Recording Equipment: Nakamichi CM-100 mics with CP-4 Shotgun caps > Sony D-5 [10]. Also: Microphones appear hand-held, causing occasional stereo left and right drift [30]
- **gd1984-10-09.senn421.pauline.miller.91410.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Rick Pauline; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Sennheiser 421 -> Cassette Master (Sony D5/Maxell XLII-S90) D [11]
- **gd1984-10-09.beyerm88.suraci.77880.flac16**: taped by Tony Suraci; transferred by Tony Suraci; source: FOB/Beyer M88>Sony D5 [12]. Also: Eugene provided the microphones for this front-of-house recording; This is the 16-bit version; the 24-bit version is on DVDA [12]
